label: TP
reason: User input flows directly to the HTML output sink via string concatenation. Although a basic sanitization step replaces double quotes with HTML entities, it fails to neutralize other malicious payloads (e.g., <script>, javascript:) that can still execute in browsers. Effective mitigation requires comprehensive encoding (e.g., esapi encoder), not selective character replacement.

evidence.note: User input flows to sink via concatenation; weak replace only handles quotes, leaving other XSS vectors active
